title: Group Discussion
description: Win the GD round: stake a position, build on and challenge others, facilitate, and drive a group to consensus. B2 to C1.

nodes.title: Stake a Clear Position
nodes.skill: Open on a debate topic with an unambiguous stance in one or two sentences.
nodes.teach_focus: Commit to a side; avoid fence-sitting; state the position before the reasons.
nodes.success_criteria: A clear, committed position on the topic, stated up front without hedging.

nodes.title: Support With Evidence
nodes.skill: Back a position with a relevant fact, example, or analogy — not just assertion.
nodes.teach_focus: Position -> because -> concrete support; prefer specifics over generalities.
nodes.success_criteria: A stance followed by at least one relevant, concrete piece of support.

nodes.title: Enter the Discussion
nodes.skill: Break into an ongoing discussion politely and claim speaking space.
nodes.teach_focus: Signal phrases to interject; assertive but not rude; link to what was just said.
nodes.success_criteria: A polite, well-timed entry that connects to the prior speaker and adds something new.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use one entry phrase: 'If I could add to that, ___.'

nodes.title: Build on Another's Point
nodes.skill: Extend a point someone else made, crediting them and adding new value.
nodes.teach_focus: Acknowledge -> extend -> add; collaborative tone that raises group quality.
nodes.success_criteria: A contribution that credits the prior speaker and meaningfully extends their idea.
nodes.bridge_focus: Finish: 'Building on what ___ said, we could also ___.'

nodes.title: Disagree Respectfully
nodes.skill: Challenge another participant's point without attacking the person.
nodes.teach_focus: Concede something valid -> state the counter -> keep it about ideas.
nodes.success_criteria: A disagreement that concedes a fair point, states a clear counter, and stays civil.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'That's fair, but I'd push back because ___.'

nodes.title: Present a Balanced View
nodes.skill: Weigh both sides of the topic, then land on a reasoned position.
nodes.teach_focus: Acknowledge the strongest opposing point honestly before concluding; show nuance.
nodes.success_criteria: A nuanced contribution that fairly states a counter-argument and still reaches a clear conclusion.
nodes.bridge_focus: Name one point for each side, then say which is stronger.

nodes.title: Steer a Derailed Discussion
nodes.skill: Redirect a discussion that has drifted off-topic back to the core question.
nodes.teach_focus: Name the drift neutrally; restate the actual question; offer a refocusing point.
nodes.success_criteria: A move that gently flags the drift and pulls the group back to the original topic.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'We've drifted a bit — the real question is ___.'

nodes.title: Bring In Quieter Voices
nodes.skill: Invite a silent participant into the discussion to show facilitation skill.
nodes.teach_focus: Notice who hasn't spoken; invite without pressure; reference the topic for them.
nodes.success_criteria: A natural, specific invitation that opens space for a quieter participant.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'I'd like to hear ___'s take on this.'

nodes.title: Manage a Dominant Speaker
nodes.skill: Tactfully reclaim the floor from someone monopolizing the discussion.
nodes.teach_focus: Validate briefly -> interrupt cleanly -> hand off; assertive without hostility.
nodes.success_criteria: A polite but firm move that pauses the dominant speaker and redistributes the floor.
nodes.bridge_focus: Use: 'That's a strong point — let's also hear other views.'

nodes.title: Summarize and Drive Consensus
nodes.skill: Synthesize the group's points into a summary that moves toward a shared conclusion.
nodes.teach_focus: Capture the main threads fairly; name common ground; propose a conclusion.
nodes.success_criteria: A concise synthesis of the discussion's key points plus a proposed consensus the group can rally around.
nodes.bridge_focus: Name the two main points raised, then propose where the group agrees.
